definitions.explanation: A telephone line connecting to outside the building or organization, as opposed to an internal extension line. In Japanese offices, you typically dial a number (often 0) to access an outside line.

examples.japanese: {外線|がいせん}にかけるには０を{押|お}してください。
examples.english: To call an outside line, please press 0.

examples.japanese: {外線|がいせん}が{鳴|な}っているから{取|と}ってくれる？
examples.english: The outside line is ringing — can you get it?

examples.japanese: {会議中|かいぎちゅう}は{外線|がいせん}を{受付|うけつけ}に{転送|てんそう}するように{設定|せってい}してある。
examples.english: During meetings, outside calls are set to be forwarded to reception.

notes:
USAGE:
{外線|がいせん} is standard office vocabulary in Japan. Most business phone systems distinguish between {外線|がいせん} (outside lines) and {内線|ないせん} (internal extensions). Knowing this distinction is essential for working in a Japanese office.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外線|がいせん}をかける (to make an outside call)
- {外線|がいせん}が{入|はい}る (an outside call comes in)
- {外線|がいせん}{番号|ばんごう} (outside line number)
- {外線|がいせん}に{出|で}る (to answer an outside call)

RELATED WORDS:
- {内線|ないせん}: internal extension line
- {代表電話|だいひょうでんわ}: main phone number (of a company)
- {転送|てんそう}: call forwarding
